title: Three equivalents of a scheme having affine diagonal: affine pairwise intersections of affine opens, or existence of an open covering whose all finite intersections are affine; in particular any separated scheme satisfies them.
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter coherent.tex (Cohomology of Schemes)

difficulty_reason: The full cycle is in the span. (1)=>(2): for affine opens U, V the intersection U cap V equals Delta^{-1}(U x V), which is affine because the diagonal is assumed affine; (2)=>(3) is recorded as immediate. (3)=>(1): the products U_i x U_i' form an affine open covering of X x X and Delta^{-1}(U_i x U_i') = U_i cap U_i' is affine by the covering hypothesis, so Delta is affine by the named pointwise characterisation of affine morphisms (Morphisms, Lemma morphisms-lemma-characterize-affine) applied to that covering - the covering check is written out in the span and only the standard characterisation is cited by name. The final separated case follows from the cited Schemes criterion (schemes-lemma-characterize-separated), again a named routine finish.
